walkthroughs.h2: "Fair is foul, and foul is fair"
walkthroughs.body_html:
The witches' chant uses antithesis — pairing opposites.

It establishes the play's moral confusion: nothing is as it seems. It's also a key motif echoed by Macbeth himself.

Macbeth asks: "Will all great Neptune's ocean wash this blood / Clean from my hand?"

Blood becomes a symbol of guilt. Lady Macbeth's "Out, damned spot!" returns to the same motif.

"Is this a dagger which I see before me?" is a soliloquy revealing Macbeth's tortured mind.

The dagger may be supernatural — or a hallucination. Shakespeare keeps it ambiguous.
